notes: Document roles: 2018_04 and 2018_05 are the University-wide frameworks (Dec 2015, in force on the reference date per their metadata) setting a floor for every School's full-time ladder faculty; 2018_00 (FAS Handbook ch. 3H) and 2018_02 (ch. 3A) are the FAS implementation (FAS covers arts and sciences and SEAS, so it is main campus under V3); 2018_01 is the FAS request form for Parental Teaching Relief (consistent with the Handbook); 2018_03 is a navigation page with links only, no policy.

V3c: where the FAS Handbook and the University-wide framework state the same benefit (FMLA, MPLA, eight-week childbirth medical leave, six-month medical leave, workload reduction / Parental Teaching Relief), one component cites both. The tenure-clock extension differs (framework: primary caregivers only; FAS: either parent, automatic), so the framework version (c8) is the main-campus component and the FAS version (c9) is recorded by unit and linked concurrent_with c8. The FAS medical and personal clock extensions, personal leave and paid sick time have no University-wide counterpart and are coded as main-campus provisions.

Workload reduction / Parental Teaching Relief: the framework defers the form of the reduction to each School ('as defined by the School'; for Schools with significant teaching responsibilities, Parental Teaching Relief); the FAS definition (teaching only; service and advising continue; research up to the faculty member) supplies the relief fields. The framework states the limit of two birth or adoption events (use_limit). No pay level is stated for the relief (framework calls the package 'paid parental leave'), so R3's ambiguous flag is set.

Other groups (not tenure-stream), recorded in notes: College Fellows and multi-year preceptors, lecturers and Briggs-Copeland Lecturers receive eight weeks of paid medical leave (including the eight-week childbirth leave) but are not eligible for parental teaching relief; dependent lectureships follow staff or research policies. Senior preceptors and senior lecturers receive relief for the remainder of the semester (c15).

FMLA eligibility: FAS deems faculty eligible after at least half-time appointment in the FAS for three consecutive months (more generous than the statute's 12 months and 1,250 hours). Harvard continues the employer health-insurance contribution during FMLA leave (not pay).

Leave limit: 'no faculty member will be eligible for more than two consecutive terms of relief from full-time departmental teaching duties' (ordinary application; family and research leaves) recorded as 32 weeks; also 'Ordinarily, faculty members should not be out of the Harvard classroom for more than a year at a time' and APH 3A 'Leaves may not be granted for more than one year at a time' (not recorded as a limit; a per-leave maximum used as c12's length).
Calendar: semesters stated ('one semester or half-time duty for two semesters'; 'up to one semester'); length not stated, so calendar.kind = semester, and the term length follows R8's order.

Chain, birth parent: medical leave of absence up to 6 months (c4) containing its pay (c5) and, from its start, the 8-week childbirth medical leave (c3, within c4); FMLA 12 (c1) and MPLA 8 (c2) concurrent from the start (4 unpaid FMLA weeks after the 8 paid); parental teaching relief 1 semester (c6, or c7 half over two terms in lieu) also_available with c3 (order not fixed); LTD (c14) consecutive_after the six-month paid medical leave (c5).

Chain, non-birth parent: FMLA 12 (c1) with MPLA 8 (c2) concurrent; parental teaching relief 1 semester for a primary caregiver (c6, or c7 in lieu), not linked to FMLA (its also_available link to c3 does not count for this role).

Cited but not saved: Massachusetts Parental Leave Act text; Massachusetts Paid Sick Time Law text; existing Harvard sick leave policies (APH 3A(5)); Harvard long-term disability (LTD) coverage information (Harvard Benefits Office); each School's Faculty Handbook (framework; only FAS saved); FAS APH ch. 3B Short-Term Absence during Term Time, 3C-3E research leaves, 3F Leaves for Non-Ladder Faculty Members, 3G Leaves of Absence for Public Service, 3I Family Leave Policy for Postdoctoral Fellows and Research Associates (navigation links; not faculty parental provisions as far as titles show); FAS APH Chapter 2 (compensation). The FAS PTR application URL in the Handbook is the saved form 2018_01.
